tastingNotes: Very sweet high-corn bourbon with maple/honey and toasted marshmallow notes, featuring rounded oak from the lower entry proof.
notes: Used primarily in the 65x-72x barrel range. This mashbill was discontinued but represents some of Willett's earliest post-2012 distillate.

tastingNotes: Rich and sweet with intense caramel, maple and marshmallow sweetness, complemented by stronger oak spice and tannin from the higher entry proof.
notes: Same grain bill as the low entry version but barreled at 125 proof, resulting in more oak influence and structure.

tastingNotes: Classic Kentucky bourbon profile with vanilla, caramel, brown sugar, baking spice, cherry and dark fruit notes, balanced oak.
notes: This is Willett's core bourbon mashbill, used across many barrel ranges. It represents a traditional bourbon recipe with moderate rye content.

tastingNotes: Dessert-leaning profile with caramel sauce, cinnamon-cereal, chocolate, and rich fruit notes; softer spice due to wheat instead of rye.
notes: Wheated bourbons replace the rye with wheat, creating a sweeter, softer character. Some experimental variations include cured oak finishes.

tastingNotes: Spicier, more herbal and peppery than the original mashbill; still has caramel and vanilla sweetness, plus baking spice and sometimes citrus peel.
notes: With 38% rye, this is a high-rye bourbon that bridges the gap between traditional bourbon and rye whiskey character.

tastingNotes: Bold rye spice with brandied/dark cherry, cola, cinnamon and baking spice, featuring a long, assertive finish.
notes: This is Willett's flagship rye mashbill with 74% rye grain, producing an intensely spicy and complex rye whiskey.

tastingNotes: Gentler rye with a mix of vanilla and caramel sweetness alongside rye herbal and minty notes; less aggressive spice than the high rye rye.
notes: With 51% rye and 34% corn, this barely-legal rye whiskey offers more sweetness and approachability than the high-rye version.

tastingNotes: Layered cereal and bread notes from all four grains, medium sweetness, and balanced baking spice.
notes: A unique four-grain mashbill (55/12/18/15) using corn, rye, wheat, and malted barley. Found primarily in the 321xx range with American oak barrels.
